info.name: FieldOps - Field Service Management API
info.description:
B7A6 Assignment 7 - Field Service Management (student ID last digit 7).

Flow: a customer raises a service request -> an admin approves it and assigns a skill-matched technician into a conflict-free slot -> the technician runs the job through a guarded status workflow and logs parts -> the system generates an invoice -> the customer pays through Stripe -> the payment is confirmed by a signature-verified webhook.

Run the folders top to bottom. Auth captures the role tokens automatically, and Catalog / Sites / Technicians capture the ids the request flow needs, so no manual copying is required.

Demo admin: admin@gmail.com / Admin@12345

request.description: One route, two audiences: ADMIN sees every request, CUSTOMER only their own. The scoping lives in the service layer, never in the route.
searchTerm matches code, title and description, case-insensitively.
Refused once a dispatcher has acted on the request.
Customer only, PENDING only.
Soft delete. Refused for CONVERTED requests, which already have a work order.

One Serializable transaction: verify the technician holds the category's required skill -> check the daily job cap -> create the WorkOrder with a WO- code -> flip the request to CONVERTED -> write history and audit rows.

Time-overlap is deliberately NOT checked in application code. The Postgres exclusion constraint no_technician_double_booking enforces it, which removes the race that two dispatchers could otherwise drive through a check-then-insert.
Role-scoped three ways: ADMIN all, TECHNICIAN own jobs, CUSTOMER own company's jobs. Filters: status, technicianId, from, to, searchTerm.
Includes the full status history.
Three gates per transition: is it legal from the current status (TRANSITIONS map), is this role allowed to drive it, and for a technician is this actually their job.
Stamps actualStart.
unitPrice is stored on the row rather than looked up later: an invoice must keep the price as it was at the time of the job.
Stamps actualEnd, which the invoice bills from.
Re-triggers the exclusion constraint: moving onto an occupied slot returns 409.

One transaction: labourHours from actualEnd - actualStart (floored at 0.5h) -> labourAmount = hours x the technician's hourlyRate -> partsAmount = sum(unitPrice x quantity) -> 15% VAT -> total. Takes an INV- number from a sequence and moves the work order to INVOICED.

All five money components are stored, not just the total, so the invoice keeps its own arithmetic even after the technician's rate changes.
Role-scoped. Filters: status, from, to, searchTerm.

Writes a Payment row in INITIATED state with our own transactionId, then creates a Stripe Checkout session carrying that id in metadata. Open the returned checkoutUrl and pay with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242, any future expiry, any CVC.

Each attempt is its own Payment row, which is why an Invoice has many Payments.

item.name: Stripe webhook (reference only - do not send from Postman)

request.description:
The only path that marks an invoice PAID. Nothing else in the codebase writes InvoiceStatus.PAID or WorkOrderStatus.PAID, and PAID has an empty role list in the transition map, so the status endpoint cannot reach it either.

Mounted in app.ts with express.raw() ahead of express.json(), because Stripe signs the raw bytes of the body.

Idempotent: the handler looks the payment up by our transactionId and returns early if it is already SUCCESS, and re-verifies the charged amount against the invoice total before settling.

Drive it locally with:
  stripe listen --forward-to localhost:5000/api/v1/payments/webhook

item.name: 09 Customer feedback

request.description:
Closes the flow. One transaction: insert the Feedback row and recompute the technician's ratingAvg / ratingCount.

Guards: the caller must be the customer whose job it was, the work order must be PAID, and only one feedback per work order (Feedback.workOrderId is @unique, so the database refuses a second row even under a race).

The average is stored on TechnicianProfile rather than aggregated on every read, which keeps the technician list a single query.

item.name: Get feedback for a work order

request.description: Ownership-checked for customers and technicians; admins see any.
Role-scoped: a customer sees the ratings they left, a technician the ratings they received, an admin everything. Filters: rating, technicianId, searchTerm.
Rating a work order that has not reached PAID is refused.

item.description: Final step of the service flow: the customer rates the completed, paid job and the technician rating is recomputed.

item.name: 401 - no token on a protected route

request.description: Expect 401.

Approve a second request onto a window overlapping an existing job for the same technician. Postgres raises SQLSTATE 23P01 from the exclusion constraint, and the global error handler maps it to 409 'Technician already has a job in this time window'.
PAID is unreachable from the status route by any role. Only the Stripe webhook sets it.
Zod failures are returned field by field in the `errors` array.
